summary: Lycksele Airport (LYC) is a regional airport serving the inland municipality of Lycksele in Västerbotten County, northern Sweden. Originally established during World War II as a military airfield, it now functions as an important transport link for the sparsely populated interior of northern Sweden. The airport supports both scheduled passenger services and general aviation, with a single main runway suited to the region's challenging subarctic climate.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate scheduled flights from Lycksele Airport?
A: Populär regional carrier Amapola Flyg has historically operated routes connecting Lycksele to Stockholm, though schedules and operators may vary by season. Check with current carriers for the latest timetable.

Q: How far is the airport from Lycksele town center?
A: The airport is located only a few kilometers from central Lycksele, making it a quick drive for most travelers.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Rental car availability is typically limited at this regional airport; travelers are advised to arrange vehicles in advance or check with local providers in Lycksele.

Q: What is the best time to fly to Lycksele for good weather?
A: Summer months (June through August) offer the mildest conditions and longest daylight hours, while winter flights offer views of the snowy landscape but may face weather-related delays.
transport_tips: Lycksele Airport is located just outside the town, so a short taxi ride is the most convenient option for reaching the town center. Public transport options are limited, so arranging a rental car or pre-booked taxi in advance is recommended during winter months. The E12 highway passes near Lycksele, providing onward road connections to Umeå and other regional destinations.
local_tip: If traveling in winter, build in extra buffer time for your return journey—the airport's location in inland Lapland means it can experience heavy snowfall and reduced visibility, even when coastal airports further north remain clearer.
